{{Short description|Metric used to assess image quality}}
The '''Fréchet inception distance (FID)''' is a [[Metric (mathematics)|metric]] used to assess the quality of images created by a [[Generative AI|generative model]], like a [[generative adversarial network]] (GAN)<ref name="fid">{{cite journal |last1=Heusel |first1=Martin |last2=Ramsauer |first2=Hubert |last3=Unterthiner |first3=Thomas |last4=Nessler |first4=Bernhard |last5=Hochreiter |first5=Sepp |title=GANs Trained by a Two Time-Scale Update Rule Converge to a Local Nash Equilibrium |journal=Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems |date=2017 |volume=30 |arxiv=1706.08500 |url=https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2017/hash/8a1d694707eb0fefe65871369074926d-Abstract.html |language=en}}</ref> or a [[diffusion model]].<ref name="classifier-free-diffusion" /><ref name=":0">{{cite arXiv |last1=Esser |first1=Patrick |title=Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis |date=2024-03-05 |eprint=2403.03206 |last2=Kulal |first2=Sumith |last3=Blattmann |first3=Andreas |last4=Entezari |first4=Rahim |last5=Müller |first5=Jonas |last6=Saini |first6=Harry |last7=Levi |first7=Yam |last8=Lorenz |first8=Dominik |last9=Sauer |first9=Axel|class=cs.CV }}</ref> 

The FID compares the distribution of generated images with the distribution of a set of real images (a "ground truth" set).  Rather than comparing individual images, [[mean]] and [[covariance]] statistics of many images generated by the model are compared with the same statistics generated from images in the ground truth or reference set.  A [[convolutional neural network]] such as an [[Inception (deep learning architecture)|inception]] architecture is used to produce higher-level features describing the images, thus leading to the name Fréchet ''inception'' distance.

The FID is inspired by the earlier [[inception score]] (IS) metric which evaluates only the distribution of generated images.<ref name="fid" /> The FID metric does not replace the IS metric; classifiers that achieve the best (lowest) FID score tend to have greater sample variety while classifiers achieving the best (highest) IS score tend to have better quality within individual images.<ref name="classifier-free-diffusion">{{cite arXiv |last1=Ho |first1=Jonathan |last2=Salimans |first2=Tim |title=Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance |date=2022 |class=cs.LG |eprint=2207.12598}}</ref>

The FID metric was introduced in 2017,<ref name="fid" /> and is the current standard metric for assessing the quality of models that generate synthetic images as of 2024.  It has been used to measure the quality of many recent models including the high-resolution StyleGAN1<ref name="stylegan1">{{cite journal |last1=Karras |first1=Tero |last2=Laine |first2=Samuli |last3=Aila |first3=Timo |year=2020 |title=A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks |journal=IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence |volume=PP |issue=12 |pages=4217–4228 |arxiv=1812.04948 |doi=10.1109/TPAMI.2020.2970919 |pmid=32012000 |s2cid=211022860}}</ref> and StyleGAN2<ref>{{cite arXiv |eprint=1912.04958 |class=cs.CV |first1=Tero |last1=Karras |first2=Samuli |last2=Laine |title=Analyzing and Improving the Image Quality of StyleGAN |date=23 March 2020 |last3=Aittala |first3=Miika |last4=Hellsten |first4=Janne |last5=Lehtinen |first5=Jaakko |last6=Aila |first6=Timo}}</ref> networks, and diffusion models.<ref name="classifier-free-diffusion" /><ref name=":0" />

The FID attempts to compare images visually through deep layers of an inception network. More recent works take this further by instead comparing [[Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training|CLIP]] embeddings of the images.<ref>{{cite conference

== Overview ==
The purpose of the FID score is to measure the diversity of images created by a generative model with images in a reference dataset. The reference dataset could be [[ImageNet]] or COCO-2014.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Lin |first1=Tsung-Yi |title=Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context |date=2015-02-20 |last2=Maire |first2=Michael |last3=Belongie |first3=Serge |last4=Bourdev |first4=Lubomir |last5=Girshick |first5=Ross |last6=Hays |first6=James |last7=Perona |first7=Pietro |last8=Ramanan |first8=Deva |last9=Zitnick |first9=C. Lawrence|class=cs.CV |eprint=1405.0312 }}</ref> Using a large dataset as a reference is important as the reference image set should represent the full diversity of images which the model attempts to create.

Generative models such as [[diffusion models]] produce novel images that have features from the reference set, but are themselves quite different from any image in the training set.  So the quality of these models cannot be assessed by simply comparing each image to an image in the training set pixel-by-pixel, as done, for example, with the [[Norm (mathematics)|L2 norm]].

Instead, the FID models the two sets of images as if they were drawn from two [[multivariate normal distribution|multidimensional Gaussian distributions]] <math>\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma)</math> and <math>\mathcal{N}(\mu',\Sigma')</math>.  The distance between the two distributions is calculated as the [[Wasserstein distance|2-Wasserstein distance]] between the two Gaussian distributions.

Rather than directly comparing images pixel by pixel (for example, as done by the [[L2 norm]]), the FID compares the mean and standard deviation of the deepest layer in [[Inceptionv3|Inception v3]] (the 2048-dimensional activation vector of its last [[pooling layer]].) These layers are closer to output nodes that correspond to real-world objects such as a specific breed of dog or an airplane, and further from the shallow layers near the input image. So the FID compares how often the same high-level features are found within the two sets of images.
After every image has been processed through the inception architecture, the means and covariances of the activation of the last layer on the two datasets are compared with the distance<math display="block"> d_{F}(\mathcal N(\mu, \Sigma), \mathcal N(\mu', \Sigma'))^2 = \lVert \mu - \mu' \rVert^2_2 + \operatorname{tr}\left(\Sigma + \Sigma' -2\left(\Sigma \Sigma'  \right)^\frac{1}{2} \right)</math>Higher distances indicate a poorer generative model. A score of 0 indicates a perfect model.

== Formal definition ==
For any two probability distributions <math> \mu, \nu</math> over <math>\R^n</math> having finite mean and variances, their [[Fréchet distance]] is<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fréchet. |first1=M |date=1957 |title=Sur la distance de deux lois de probabilité. ("On the distance between two probability laws") |journal=C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris |volume=244 |pages=689–692 |quote=translated abstract: The author indicates an explicit expression of the distance of two probability laws, according to the first definition of Paul Lévy. He also indicates a convenient modification of this definition.}}</ref><math display="block">d_F (\mu, \nu):=\left( \inf_{\gamma \in \Gamma (\mu, \nu)} \int_{\R^n \times \R^n} \|x-y\|^2 \, \mathrm{d} \gamma (x, y) \right)^{1/2},</math>where <math>\Gamma(\mu, \nu)</math> is the set of all measures on <math>\R^n \times \R^n</math> with [[Marginal distribution|marginals]] ''<math>\mu</math>'' and ''<math>\nu</math>'' on the first and second factors respectively. (The set <math>\Gamma(\mu,\nu)</math> is also called the set of all '''[[Coupling (probability)|couplings]]''' of ''<math>\mu</math>'' and ''<math>\nu</math>''.). 

For two [[multivariate normal distribution|multidimensional Gaussian distributions]] <math>\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma)</math> and <math>\mathcal{N}(\mu',\Sigma')</math>, it is expressed in closed form as<ref name="gaussian">{{cite journal |last1=Dowson |first1=D. C |last2=Landau |first2=B. V |date=1 September 1982 |title=The Fréchet distance between multivariate normal distributions |journal=Journal of Multivariate Analysis |language=en |volume=12 |issue=3 |pages=450–455 |doi=10.1016/0047-259X(82)90077-X |issn=0047-259X |doi-access=free}}</ref><math display="block"> d_{F}(\mathcal N(\mu, \Sigma), \mathcal N(\mu', \Sigma'))^2 = \lVert \mu - \mu' \rVert^2_2 + \operatorname{tr}\left(\Sigma + \Sigma' -2\left(\Sigma \Sigma'  \right)^\frac{1}{2} \right)</math>This allows us to define the FID in [[pseudocode]] form:<blockquote>'''INPUT''' a function <math>f: \Omega_X \to \R^n</math>.

'''INPUT''' two datasets <math>S, S'\subset \Omega_X</math>.

Compute <math>f(S), f(S') \subset \R^n</math>.

Fit two gaussian distributions <math>\mathcal N(\mu, \Sigma), \mathcal N(\mu', \Sigma')</math>, respectively for <math>f(S), f(S')</math>.

'''RETURN''' <math>d_{F}(\mathcal N(\mu, \Sigma), \mathcal N(\mu', \Sigma'))^2</math>.</blockquote>In most practical uses of the FID, <math>\Omega_X</math> is the space of images, and <math>f</math> is an [[Inceptionv3|Inception v3]] model trained on the [[ImageNet]], but without its final classification layer. Technically, it is the 2048-dimensional activation vector of its last [[pooling layer]]. Of the two datasets <math>S, S' </math>, one of them is a reference dataset, which could be the ImageNet itself, and the other is a set of images generated by a [[Generative AI|generative model]], such as [[Generative adversarial network|GAN]], or [[diffusion model]].<ref name="fid" />

== Variants ==
Specialized variants of FID have been suggested as evaluation metric for music enhancement algorithms as '''Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD)''',<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kilgour |first1=Kevin |last2=Zuluaga |first2=Mauricio |last3=Roblek |first3=Dominik |last4=Sharifi |first4=Matthew |title=Fréchet Audio Distance: A Reference-Free Metric for Evaluating Music Enhancement Algorithms |journal=Interspeech 2019 |date=2019-09-15 |pages=2350–2354 |doi=10.21437/Interspeech.2019-2219|s2cid=202725406 }}</ref> for generative models of video as '''Fréchet Video Distance (FVD)''',<ref>{{cite journal |website=Open Review |last1=Unterthiner |first1=Thomas |last2=Steenkiste |first2=Sjoerd van |last3=Kurach |first3=Karol |last4=Marinier |first4=Raphaël |last5=Michalski |first5=Marcin |last6=Gelly |first6=Sylvain |title=FVD: A new Metric for Video Generation |date=2019-03-27 |url=https://openreview.net/forum?id=rylgEULtdN |language=en}}</ref> and for AI-generated molecules as '''Fréchet ChemNet Distance (FCD)'''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Preuer |first1=Kristina |last2=Renz |first2=Philipp |last3=Unterthiner |first3=Thomas |last4=Hochreiter |first4=Sepp |last5=Klambauer |first5=Günter |title=Fréchet ChemNet Distance: A Metric for Generative Models for Molecules in Drug Discovery |journal=Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling |date=2018-09-24 |volume=58 |issue=9 |pages=1736–1741 |doi=10.1021/acs.jcim.8b00234|pmid=30118593 |arxiv=1803.09518 |s2cid=51892387 }}</ref>

== Limitations ==
Chong and Forsyth<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Chong |first1=Min Jin |last2=Forsyth |first2=David |date=2020-06-15 |title=Effectively Unbiased FID and Inception Score and where to find them |class=cs.CV |eprint=1911.07023 }}</ref> showed FID to be statistically biased, in the sense that their expected value over a finite data is not their true value. 
Also, because FID measured the Wasserstein distance towards the ground-truth distribution, it is inadequate for evaluating the quality of generators in domain adaptation setups, or in zero-shot generation. 
Finally, while FID is more consistent with human judgment than previously used inception score, 
there are cases where FID is inconsistent with human judgment.<ref name=":1">{{cite arXiv |eprint=1803.07474 |class=cs.CV |first1=Shaohui |last1=Liu |first2=Yi |last2=Wei |title=An Improved Evaluation Framework for Generative Adversarial Networks |date=2018-07-19 |last3=Lu |first3=Jiwen |last4=Zhou |first4=Jie}}</ref> In Liu et al., FID rated the pixelation or swapping of patches of images more highly than the addition of random noise,<ref name=":1" />{{Rp|page=10}} and could be increased by [[adversarial noise]].<ref name=":1" />{{Rp|page=14}}
